hints: Look first at the carbon holding the halogen in each molecule, is it primary or tertiary?
Remember that 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2Cl$, is primary, while 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, $CH_3CH_2C(Br)(CH_3)_2$, is tertiary.
Link the faster SN1 reaction of the stable tertiary carbocation and weaker C-Br bond to which precipitate time, T1 or T2, will be shorter.
walkthrough:
**Draw and classify the halogenoalkanes**

Think like a detective. Find the C-X carbon and count how many other carbons join to it.

$$\text{1-chloro-2-methylpropane: } (CH_3)_2CHCH_2Cl \text{, primary}$$
$$\text{2-bromo-2-methylbutane: } CH_3CH_2C(Br)(CH_3)_2 \text{, tertiary}$$

**Assign the main mechanism**

Primary halogenoalkanes have little hindrance but form very unstable carbocations, so they favour $S_N2$. Tertiary halogenoalkanes are hindered but form stable carbocations, so they favour $S_N1$.

$$\text{primary } RCH_2Cl \rightarrow S_N2$$
$$\text{tertiary } R_3CBr \rightarrow S_N1$$

**Compare the rates and precipitate times**

The silver nitrate test gives $AgCl$ or $AgBr$ precipitate when $Cl^-$ or $Br^-$ is released. Faster substitution means shorter time.

Two factors make the tertiary bromide much faster: a tertiary carbocation is stabilised by induction and hyperconjugation, and $C-Br$ is weaker and breaks more easily than $C-Cl$. So T2 is short and T1 is long, meaning $T_1 > T_2$.

**Pick the fully correct row**

We need the row where compound, its correct mechanism, and the correct time comparison all match. Only the row for 1-chloro-2-methylpropane with $S_N2$ and $T_1 > T_2$ fits perfectly.

options.A: Incorrect. 1-chloro-2-methylpropane is primary so its main mechanism is SN2, not SN1. The time is also wrong because the primary chloride is slower, so T1 is longer, not shorter, than T2.
options.B: Correct. 1-chloro-2-methylpropane is primary, so SN2 is right. It reacts much more slowly than the tertiary bromide because it cannot form a stable carbocation and C-Cl is stronger than C-Br, so its precipitate time T1 is longer than T2, giving T1 > T2.
options.C: Trap. The mechanism part is right for 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, it is tertiary so SN1 is correct. But the time part is backwards. The tertiary bromide is very fast, so T2 is short, not long. T2 > T1 is false.
options.D: Incorrect. Although the time comparison T1 > T2 is true, the mechanism for 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is wrong. A tertiary halogenoalkane goes mainly by SN1 due to the stable tertiary carbocation, not SN2 which is blocked by steric hindrance.
